notes_kept_out.fact: For a certificate issued retrospectively, the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.

passages.title: Origin criteria: wholly obtained or product-specific rule

quotes.text: is wholly obtained or produced in the territory of the Party as per Article 3.3
has undergone sufficient working or production as per the Product Specific Rules (PSR) in Annex 3B.
Notwithstanding paragraph 1 above, the final manufacture before export must have occurred in the Party of export.

passages.summary: A product originates in the UAE, and can receive the CEPA rate, if it is either (a) wholly obtained or produced in the UAE, or (b) meets its product-specific rule in Annex 3B (in India: Annexure-B of Notification 39/2022). The two routes are alternatives. The final manufacture before export must take place in the UAE. No default rule was found for a product without a product-specific rule.

passages.title: Value-addition formulas (build-down and build-up)
passages.provision: AGR Art. 3.2.2; R39 Rule 3(2); Annexure-B Rule 1(f)

quotes.text: The producer or manufacturer has the option to use either of the following two methods
(FOB value or Ex Works price) − (Value of NOM) / FOB value or Ex Works price
Cost of originating material + direct labour cost + direct overhead cost / FOB value or Ex Works price

passages.summary: Value addition may be calculated either by build-down, (FOB value or Ex-Works price minus the value of non-originating materials) divided by the same price, or by build-up, (originating materials plus direct labour plus direct overhead) divided by the same price. Product-specific rule percentages are on an FOB basis; on an Ex-Works basis the threshold is 5 percentage points lower, except for HS 71, which must use FOB.
notes: 'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

passages.title: Valuing non-originating materials
passages.provision: AGR Art. 3.1 and 3.10; R39 Rules 2(t), 2(zb) and 11

quotes.text: the customs value at the time of importation of the non-originating materials used, i.e., the CIF value
the first ascertainable price paid for the materials in the territory of a Party.

passages.summary: Non-originating materials are materials whose country of origin is neither the UAE nor India. They are valued at their customs (CIF) value at import; if that is unknown, at the first ascertainable price paid for them in the UAE or India. Indirect materials (such as fuel, tools and consumables used in production) count as neither originating nor non-originating.

passages.title: Minimal operations that never confer origin

quotes.text: a product shall not be considered originating in a Party by merely undergoing any of the following operations
“simple” describes an activity which needs neither special skills / nor machines, apparatus or equipment especially produced or installed to carry out the activity.

items.text: operations to ensure the preservation of products in good condition during transport, and storage / (such as drying, freezing or thawing, keeping in brine …)
changes of packaging and breaking up and assembly of packages;
washing, cleaning, removal of dust, oxide, oil, paint or other coverings;
for textiles: attaching accessory articles such as straps, bands, beads, cords, rings and eyelets; / ironing or pressing of textiles;
husking, partial or total bleaching, polishing, and glazing of cereals and rice;
operations to colour sugar or form sugar lumps;
peeling and removal of stones and shells from fruits, nuts and vegetables;
sharpening, simple grinding or simple cutting;
simple operations such as removal of dust, sifting, screening, sorting, classifying, grading, matching;
simple placing in bottles, cans, flasks, bags, cases, boxes, fixing on cards or boards / and all other simple packaging operations;
affixing or printing marks, labels, logos and other like distinguishing signs on products or their packaging;
simple mixing of products, whether or not of different kinds;
simple assembly of parts of articles to constitute a complete article or disassembly of products into parts;
simple testing, calibration, inspection or certification; or
any combination of two or more operations in subparagraphs (a) to (p) above.

passages.summary: The operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says. 'Simple' means the activity needs no special skills and no machines or equipment specially made or installed for it. Items most relevant to traders and re-exporters: repacking (b), simple packaging (k), labelling (l), simple assembly (n) and simple testing (p).
notes: A product that only undergoes these operations does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.

passages.title: De minimis tolerance

quotes.text: their total value does not exceed ten percent (10%) of the FOB value or Ex Works price of the exported product; or
is less than seven percent (7%) of the total weight of the materials used in the production of the exported
In the case of a wholly obtained product, a de minimis value not exceeding one percent (1%)

passages.summary: A small amount of non-originating material is tolerated: up to 10% of the FOB value or Ex-Works price; for textiles in HS chapters 50 to 63, less than 7% of the total weight of materials; for wholly obtained products, up to 1%.
notes: By interpretation, de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.
dev_notes: The Art. 3.4.1 lead-in (the exact conditions) was not captured verbatim.

passages.title: Bilateral cumulation
passages.summary: Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.

passages.title: Direct consignment and third-party invoicing

step.en: Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations there other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. If a third party issues the invoice, indicate 'third-party invoicing'.
step.ar: اشحن البضائع مباشرة من الإمارات إلى الهند. ولا يُسمح بالعبور عبر بلد آخر إلا تحت رقابة الجمارك، ودون أي عمليات هناك سوى التفريغ وإعادة التحميل والتخزين أو ما شابه. وإذا أصدر طرف ثالث الفاتورة، فاذكر عبارة 'third-party invoicing' (فوترة طرف ثالث).

quotes.text: An importing Party shall not deny a claim for preferential tariff treatment for the sole reason that an invoice

passages.summary: Preference is given only to originating goods shipped directly from the UAE to India. Transit through another country is allowed only under customs control, with no operations other than unloading, reloading, storage or similar. An invoice issued by a third party does not by itself cause the claim to be denied; the exporter must indicate 'third-party invoicing'.

passages.title: Certificate of origin: validity, timing and form

step.en: Have the certificate issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. It is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import (it can list several products).
step.ar: احرص على إصدار الشهادة قبل التصدير أو عنده أو خلال 5 أيام عمل منه. وهي صالحة لمدة 12 شهراً من تاريخ إصدارها وتغطي عملية استيراد واحدة (ويمكن أن تشمل عدة منتجات).

passages.provision: AGR Art. 3.13-3.14; R39 Rules 14-15 and Annexure-E

quotes.text: A Certificate of Origin shall be valid for twelve (12) months from the date of issue in the exporting Party.
The Certificate of Origin shall be valid for only one import and shall include one or more products.
shall be issued prior to, at or within five (5) working days of the date of exportation.
It shall bear the authorised signature and official seal of the competent authority.

passages.summary: A certificate of origin is valid for 12 months from issue and covers one import (it may list several products). It should be issued before, at, or within 5 working days of export. A certificate may be issued retrospectively up to 12 months from the date of shipment, marked 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' in box 9 (Remarks) of India's certificate form. Minor typing or formatting errors are tolerated; discrepancies in signature or seal are not. A lost certificate can be replaced by a certified true copy.

passages.title: What the certificate application must contain

step.en: In the application, give the HS code, description, quantity and value of the product. Each item on the certificate must qualify separately. The issuing authority may ask for detailed cost sheets or visit the factory.
step.ar: اذكر في الطلب رمز النظام المنسق (HS) ووصف المنتج وكميته وقيمته. يجب أن يستوفي كل بند في الشهادة شروط المنشأ بمفرده. وقد تطلب جهة الإصدار كشوف تكاليف مفصلة أو تزور المصنع.

quotes.text: each item must qualify separately in its own right.
detailed cost sheets, and conducting a factory visit.

passages.summary: The application, which can be submitted electronically, must include the HS code, description, quantity and value of the exported product. Each item on the certificate must qualify separately. The issuing authority may apply risk management, including asking for detailed cost sheets and visiting the factory.

passages.title: Record keeping and verification

step.en: Keep your origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year in which the certificate was issued. India may ask the UAE authority to verify the certificate, and refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying the preference.
step.ar: احتفظ بسجلات المنشأ، بما فيها تفصيل التكاليف، لمدة 5 سنوات على الأقل من نهاية السنة الميلادية التي صدرت فيها الشهادة. وقد تطلب الهند من الجهة الإماراتية التحقق من الشهادة، ويُعد رفض زيارة التحقق سبباً لرفض المعاملة التفضيلية.

quotes.text: no less than five (5) years, starting from the end of the year of the date of its issue.
Any failure to consent to a verification visit shall be grounds for a denial of preferential benefits

passages.summary: The exporter must keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years; counting from the end of the calendar year of issue satisfies both of the agreement's clocks. India may ask the UAE authority to verify a certificate; the authority answers an origin verification request within 90 days, extendable by 60. Refusing a verification visit is grounds for denying the preference.
notes: UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years govern CEPA claims.

passages.title: Who issues the preferential certificate in the UAE
passages.provision: Ministry of Foreign Trade service page; Cabinet Resolution 208/2025; R39 Annexure-D; CR 43/2022 Art. 7 and 9

quotes.text: The service allows the issuance of a preferential and non-preferential Certificate of Origin for exporting locally made products.
(b) for UAE, to the Ministry of Economy or any other agency notified from time to time;

passages.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Trade offers the e-service that issues preferential and non-preferential certificates of origin for locally made products (trade.gov.ae, 'Issue a Certificate Of Origin'), and certificate-of-origin fees are set in its fee resolution (Cabinet Resolution 208/2025). Its service page does not name India or the CEPA. The India-specific service page ('Certificate of Origin for India') is still published on the Ministry of Economy and Tourism website (moet.gov.ae). India's origin rules list the UAE issuing authority as the 'Ministry of Economy or any other agency notified from time to time'; the Ministry of Economy was renamed the Ministry of Economy and Tourism in June 2025, and no Indian update to that list was found. Chambers of commerce issue non-preferential certificates only. Ministry of Foreign Trade contact line: 171.
notes: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

passages.title: UAE e-service: Certificate of Origin for India

step.en: Apply through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service (eservices.moec.gov.ae or the smart app): log in, choose the service, fill in the form, upload proof of factory registration and the commercial invoice (a trader also uploads the factory's purchase invoice), pay the fee online and submit. Processing takes about one working day. If the application is returned with comments, correct it; once approved, print the certificate.
step.ar: قدّم الطلب عبر الخدمة الإلكترونية «شهادة المنشأ للهند» (eservices.moec.gov.ae أو التطبيق الذكي): سجّل الدخول، واختر الخدمة، واملأ النموذج، وارفع إثبات تسجيل المصنع والفاتورة التجارية (ويرفع التاجر أيضاً فاتورة الشراء من المصنع)، وادفع الرسوم إلكترونياً ثم أرسل الطلب. تستغرق المعالجة نحو يوم عمل واحد. إذا أُعيد الطلب مع ملاحظات فصحّحه، وبعد الموافقة اطبع الشهادة.

passages.provision: Ministry service pages; Cabinet Resolution 208/2025 fee schedule
passages.summary: Preferential certificates for India are requested through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service; its service page is on moet.gov.ae and links to eservices.moec.gov.ae (or the smart app). The Ministry of Foreign Trade's 'Issue a Certificate Of Origin' service (trade.gov.ae) lists the same fee bands and the same one working day. Applicants are local manufacturers and exporters whose factory is registered through Factory Registration. Documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, for a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice. Processing takes about one working day and the service runs 24/7. Fees depend on invoice value, from AED 10 to AED 200, under the Ministry of Foreign Trade fee resolution (Cabinet Resolution 208/2025). Contact listed on the India service page: 800 1222, info@moet.gov.ae.

steps: Log in to the ministry e-services portal
Choose the Certificate of Origin for India service
Receive approval, or a return with comments to correct

notes: Fee bands are in AED and apply to the invoice value in AED; no currency conversion is done by Mansha.

passages.title: Prerequisite: Factory Registration

step.en: Register your factory through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae) before you apply for the certificate. The factory must be outside a free zone and hold a MoIAT industrial licence and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added (a registration condition only, not your product's rule of origin). Registration takes about 3 working days. A trader can apply only for goods bought from a registered factory.
step.ar: سجّل مصنعك عبر خدمة تسجيل المصانع في وزارة الاقتصاد والسياحة (moet.gov.ae) قبل التقدم بطلب الشهادة. يجب أن يكون المصنع خارج المنطقة الحرة، وأن يحمل رخصة صناعية من وزارة الصناعة والتكنولوجيا المتقدمة وخطاباً منها يؤكد قيمة مضافة محلية بنسبة 40% (وهذا شرط للتسجيل فقط، وليس قاعدة المنشأ الخاصة بمنتجك). يستغرق التسجيل نحو 3 أيام عمل. ولا يجوز للتاجر التقدم إلا لبضائع مشتراة من مصنع مسجّل.

passages.actor: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism
passages.provision: Ministry of Economy and Tourism Factory Registration service page
passages.summary: Before applying for a certificate, the factory must be registered through the Ministry of Economy and Tourism's Factory Registration service (moet.gov.ae). Registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, a MoIAT industrial licence, and a MoIAT letter confirming 40% domestic value added. It takes about 3 working days. Traders can apply only for goods bought from a registered factory. The 40% value-added letter is a registration condition only; it is NOT the CEPA product-specific rule test, which is set per tariff line.
notes: A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

passages.title: Amending a certificate of origin
passages.provision: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Ministry of Economy and Tourism Amend Certificate of Origin service pages
passages.summary: An issued certificate can be amended once, for a fee of AED 20; the invoice amount and the destination cannot be changed. Both the Ministry of Foreign Trade and the Ministry of Economy and Tourism publish this service page with the same terms.

passages.title: Which Indian duties the CEPA reduces
passages.provision: N22 preamble and Table II; Customs Tariff Act s.3(7)-(9)
passages.summary: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD), and the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess only for lines in Table II. IGST, GST compensation cess and the Social Welfare Surcharge still apply, as do any anti-dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties. Because the IGST base includes BCD, a lower BCD also lowers the IGST amount.
notes: The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).

passages.title: What the Indian importer must do

step.en: Your Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry, and the importer or their customs broker uploads the certificate to e-Sanchit. Under CAROTAR 2020 the importer must hold origin information, including which origin criterion is claimed, and still has a duty of reasonable care, so you may be asked for production and cost details.
step.ar: يطالب المستورد الهندي بسعر الاتفاقية عند تقديم بيان الإدخال (bill of entry)، ويرفع المستورد أو وكيله الجمركي الشهادة إلى نظام e-Sanchit. وبموجب قواعد CAROTAR 2020 يجب أن يحتفظ المستورد بمعلومات المنشأ، بما فيها معيار المنشأ المطالب به، ويبقى عليه واجب العناية المعقولة، لذا قد يُطلب منك تقديم تفاصيل الإنتاج والتكاليف.

passages.provision: CAROTAR 2020 Rules 4-6 (official summary); CBIC Instruction 28/2022-Customs (27 Oct 2022)
passages.summary: The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020, including which origin criterion is claimed. The importer keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years from filing and must answer a customs request within 10 working days. The certificate does not remove the importer's duty of reasonable care, so the UAE exporter may be asked for production and cost details. Electronic certificates from the UAE issuing authority are accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit by the importer or customs broker.
